tour.title: The workspace at a glance
tour.description: DW SuperApps is a host-neutral control workspace that installs reusable AI Powers (gwc, ua, task-me, bmad), registers product repositories as submodules, and lets multiple agent hosts share one control plane. Start with the root README and workspace.yaml, then skim the operations guide to see the day-to-day lifecycle.

tour.title: Entering through the dw CLI
tour.description: Everything starts with bin/dw, which preflights the environment and hands off to scripts/dw_cli.py, the source-owned help entrypoint. dw_entry.py and dw_dispatch.py resolve and route subcommands, while python-resolver.sh is the shared Python launcher for Bash entrypoints.

tour.title: Powers and their manifests
tour.description: Each installed Power (gwc, ua, task-me, bmad) is declared by a YAML manifest under manifests/powers/, with power-compatibility-lock.json pinning cross-Power compatibility. The dw_power_store package implements the CLI for installing, updating, and rolling back these Powers from offline release packages.

tour.title: Power distribution pipeline
tour.description: Distributions are built from source submodules rather than branch binaries: distribution_builder.py stages Power ZIPs and full_distribution_release.py bundles them with the control plane. The installation docs and onboarding runbook walk through installing and activating a release in a fresh workspace.

tour.title: TaskController control plane (WP5)
tour.description: TaskController is the deterministic, framework-neutral A2A control plane at the heart of the workspace. The control plane layer issues only the legal ControlIntents, drives run state via engine.py and orchestrator.py, and re-derives projections after every command without touching node state directly.

tour.title: Kernel, runtime, routing, execution
tour.description: Below the control plane sits a layered core: the WP1 kernel owns legal state transitions and plan-version guards, the WP2 runtime provides an append-only journal, leases, checkpoints, and a persistence-neutral store. WP3 routing selects provider bindings purely, and WP4's execution fabric dispatches work through an immutable adapter registry.

tour.title: Host adapters and the multi-host contract
tour.description: Execution adapters implement one product-neutral port (dispatch/cancel over DispatchEnvelopes) held in an immutable registry, so Claude, Codex, Kiro, Copilot, Cline, and Kilo hosts can plug into the same runs. The shared A2A protocol doc plus the multi-host setup guides explain how one workspace stays portable across hosts.

tour.title: Interaction plane: mailboxes, wakeups, Slack cards
tour.description: The interaction package defines the reference-based A2A envelope, GitHub mailbox codec, and pointer-only wakeup semantics so executors never poll blindly. Projections bind machine state to human surfaces deterministically — including the Slack live progress card renderer and restart-safe binding snapshots.

tour.title: Project registry and submodules
tour.description: projects[] in the workspace config is the canonical registry of editable product repos, each checked out as a git submodule (.gitmodules). dw_project_registry.py manages registration and validation, dw_project_targets.py resolves project-native runtime targets, and dw-observation is the flagship example project with its own profile.

tour.title: Governance: GWC gates and validation
tour.description: Work flows through GWC-gated scrums whose designs and evidence packs live under .gwc/, keeping every change traceable to an approved gate. Validation is fail-closed: validate-workspace.py checks the whole checkout and validate-power-compatibility.py guards manifest compatibility, backed by JSON Schemas for TaskController contracts.

tour.title: Tests and CI pipelines
tour.description: Four GitHub Actions workflows guard the repo: workspace validation on push/PR, TaskController validation, the deterministic gwc-simulation-lab harness, and full-distribution release publishing. The test suite mirrors the layers you just toured — kernel, runtime, routing, packs, plus distribution and registry tests.
